statement: Nick's father advised him that whenever he feels like criticizing anyone, he should remember not everyone has had his advantages - advice Nick says has made him inclined to reserve judgment.
Nick came East, restless after the war, to learn the bond business, and rented a house in West Egg, Long Island.
Nick's house sits in West Egg, the less fashionable of the two egg-shaped peninsulas, across the bay from the more fashionable East Egg.
Tom Buchanan, Nick's old college acquaintance, had been one of the most powerful football players ever to play at New Haven.
When Nick arrives, Daisy and Jordan Baker are found reclining together on a large couch, as if just blown back in by a breeze.
When Jordan mentions that Nick must know Gatsby, Daisy reacts with surprise, asking 'What Gatsby?'
Tom enthusiastically defends a book arguing that the 'Nordic' race is losing control of civilization, revealing his anxious, bigoted worldview.
During dinner, Jordan quietly tells Nick that Tom has 'some woman in New York' - implying Tom is having an affair.
Daisy says she hopes her infant daughter will grow up to be 'a beautiful little fool,' calling that the best thing a girl can be.
Nick recalls that Jordan Baker, a professional golfer, was once at the center of an unpleasant, half-forgotten story about a tournament.
Chapter 1 ends with Nick's first glimpse of Gatsby, standing alone on his lawn and stretching his arms toward a green light across the water.
